transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, what made me come in is that my eating has just gotten all turned around lately. It's strange... some days I forget to eat lunch completely. And then other days, I'll just find myself standing at the kitchen counter eating crackers and sweets, even though, honestly, nothing really tastes right to me anyway.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or noticing that you've lost interest or pleasure in things you normally enjoy?

Yes, I have been feeling down. It's... well, most mornings I wake up with this heavy, low feeling. It's like the color has just gone out of the day before I even get dressed. I just feel very sad, to be honest.
How long have you been feeling this way—has it been a couple of weeks, or has this low mood been going on for two years or more, even if it comes and goes in intensity?
Well, it hasn't been two years. But it's been a while. I'd say this low, colorless stretch has been with me for about a year and two months now.

Over this past year and two months, has this low, down feeling been present almost every day without a break, or have there been stretches of weeks or months where your mood returned to normal in between?

Well... looking back, the sadness and just not caring about things have taken up most of this whole period. Ever since my sister became ill, it's been almost every day. Even during the times when those other strange worries about the records were quieter... the low feeling was still there. It hasn't really given me a break.

During this past year, has your low mood been severe enough to interfere with your ability to work, care for yourself, or carry out your daily responsibilities, or have you generally been able to keep functioning despite feeling down?

It has interfered, yes. I actually stopped teaching my craft classes because of it. And... well, I've been missing calls and appointments, and just family tasks that I used to handle very carefully. I still manage to stay in my home and take care of the basics, but I rely a lot more on reminders now. I just tend to put off things that used to be my normal routine.
During this past year, have you had any thoughts of worthlessness, excessive guilt, or thoughts about death or hurting yourself?

No, I don't have any plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But... I do find myself thinking sometimes that if I just didn't wake up one morning, it might be a relief to everyone. Just... easier. I don't know about guilt or feeling worthless, really, just that it wouldn't be so bad if it all just stopped.
I'm sorry, doctor, but you didn't ask me a question just now. Was there something else you wanted to know about how I've been feeling?
Earlier you mentioned some strange worries about 'the records'—can you tell me more about what that means and what those worries involve?

Well, I know it sounds odd... but I keep feeling like certain dates and names in our family papers are being changed. Or maybe hidden from me. It's like... like the hospital or someone in the family is sending me little messages through the records. I just keep seeing things that don't match up, like they're trying to tell me something by changing the details.

Have these beliefs about the records being changed or hidden happened only during the times you're feeling low and sad, or have you noticed them occurring even during periods when your mood felt more normal?

Yes, I've noticed it even when my mood is better. There was a stretch of several weeks, actually, when my mood had eased up quite a bit. I was eating again and getting dressed more normally... but I still felt sure the dates and names in the records were being changed to signal something. It didn't go away just because I felt less sad.
During this past year, has there been a period of at least two weeks where you had these beliefs about the records being changed, but were not feeling depressed at all?

Yes, like I was just saying, it was definitely longer than two weeks. It was a stretch of several weeks, really, where my mood had eased up quite a bit. I wasn't feeling depressed at all—I was back to eating and getting dressed more normally. But even during that good stretch, I still felt completely sure that the dates and names in the records were being changed to signal something to me. That part never stopped, even when my mood was fine.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates a persistent delusional belief (that family records are being altered/hidden as coded messages) that has continued unabated for several weeks even during a period when her depressive mood had fully resolved, establishing that psychotic symptoms occur independently of mood episodes for at least 2 weeks. Concurrently, she has experienced a major depressive syndrome (depressed mood, anhedonia, appetite disturbance, passive death wishes, functional impairment) that has been present for the majority (most days) of a 14-month illness duration. The combination of mood episode plus psychotic symptoms occurring both during and independent of the mood disturbance, with mood symptoms predominating over the illness course, meets criteria for Schizoaffective Disorder, depressive type (F25.1) rather than Major Depressive Disorder with psychotic features (which would require psychosis only during mood episodes) or primary psychotic disorder (which would require mood symptoms to be brief/absent relative to psychosis).
